members.name: sector_rotation_stat_arb_v1
members.universe: NIFTY Bank ETF (BANKBEES) vs NIFTY IT ETF (ITBEES) on NSE; proxy via top-2 stocks per sector
members.thesis: Indian sector indices (NIFTY Bank, NIFTY IT, NIFTY Pharma, NIFTY Auto) exhibit intraday relative value dislocations when macro news differentially impacts sectors but the market over-extrapolates the effect. For example, a rate hike fear pushes banking down 1% while IT (rate-insensitive) moves only
entry_long: spread_z < -2.0 (banking underperforming IT more than 2 sigma)
macro_shock_indicator == True (dislocation triggered by macro event)
time > 09:45 IST (allow initial volatility to settle)
entry_short: spread_z > 2.0 (banking outperforming IT more than 2 sigma)
members.exit_target: spread_z crosses 0.5 (partial reversion, don't wait for full)
members.exit_stop: spread_z exceeds 3.5 OR loss > 0.5% of capital
filters: India_VIX between 12 and 25; outside this range sector spreads too noisy
no new entries after 14:00 IST
all 4 components must have 1-min volume > 10000 shares
NIFTY 50 not limit-down or in circuit-breaker territory
avg bid-ask across 4 legs < 0.05%
weaknesses: Four-leg execution increases complexity and total slippage; each additional leg adds ~3bps slippage risk
Sector spread may not mean-revert if the macro shock is genuinely structural (e.g., sector-specific regulatory change), leading to extended drawdowns
Low trade frequency (1-2/day, only on macro event days) means the strategy may go days without signals, reducing capital efficiency
members.prior_art: Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999) industry momentum; adapted as intraday mean-reversion of sector spreads. Similar to Lo & MacKinlay (1990) contrarian profits in cross-sections.

members.name: banking_vs_it_rotation_v1
members.universe: BANK NIFTY constituents + NIFTY IT constituents
members.thesis: BANK NIFTY and NIFTY IT are the two largest sector indices by weight in NIFTY 50 and exhibit a well-documented negative intraday correlation driven by opposing macro sensitivities: banking benefits from rate cuts and domestic growth (INR strength), while IT benefits from INR weakness and global tech
entry_long: spread_zscore < -2.0 (IT outperforming, banking lagging — expect banking catch-up)
USDINR_direction <= 0 (INR not weakening further — supports banking recovery)
entry_short: spread_zscore > 2.0 (banking outperforming, IT lagging — expect IT catch-up)
USDINR_direction >= 0 (INR not strengthening further — supports IT recovery)
members.exit_target: spread_zscore reverts to 0 (spread mean reversion complete)
members.exit_stop: spread_zscore extends to ±3.0 (spread widening, stop out)
filters: India_VIX < 22; in high VIX, both sectors sell off together (positive correlation)
wait until 10:00 for stable intraday spread; stop new entries after 14:00
both sector indices trading at > 0.7x normal volume participation
skip if NIFTY 50 is moving > 1% intraday (macro dominating, rotation suppressed)
individual stock spreads < 5 bps for all 6 proxy stocks
weaknesses: The correlation regime between banking and IT is unstable — in risk-off events, both sectors sell off together and the rotation trade gets stopped out.
Using individual stocks as sector proxies introduces stock-specific risk (e.g., HDFC Bank result surprise moves the banking leg without sector-wide implication).
Very low trade frequency (1-2/day) means the strategy cannot stand alone and must be part of a portfolio of strategies.
